column1: daredevil§His daredevil reputation was built on two stunts and a photograph.§他**不怕死的**名声建立在两次特技和一张照片上。
daunt§Nothing daunted her less than a blank page.§没有什么比一张白纸更不能让她**畏惧**的了。
deadly§The silence in the room was deadly and lasted a full minute.§房间里**死一般**的寂静持续了整整一分钟。
deafen§A deafening cheer went up when the lights came back.§灯一亮，**震耳**的欢呼声就响了起来。
dearth§There is no dearth of opinions, only of evidence.§意见从不缺，**缺的是证据**。
debacle§What the papers called a debacle was, technically, a draw.§报纸称之为**溃败**的，严格说是平局。
debase§Repeating a word too often debases it.§一个词用得太滥就会**贬值**。
debatable§It is debatable whether the third volume is by the same hand.§第三卷是否出自同一人之手尚**可争论**。
debilitate§Two years of underfunding debilitated the whole department.§两年的经费不足使整个部门**元气大伤**。
debunk§Debunking a myth takes ten times the words that spreading it did.§**戳穿**一个流言所需的字数是传播它的十倍。
deceit§The deceit was discovered by a clerk checking a date.§这场**欺骗**是被一位核对日期的职员发现的。
deceitful§A deceitful summary quotes accurately and omits the sentence after.§**骗人**的摘要引用得很准确，却略去了下一句。
deceive§The eye is easily deceived by a horizon at the wrong height.§高度不对的地平线很容易**骗过**眼睛。
decimation§The decimation of the elms changed the look of every English lane.§榆树的**大批死亡**改变了英格兰每条小路的面貌。
decipher§He deciphered the label and found it was a laundry mark.§他**辨认出**那个标记，原来是洗衣店的记号。
decisive§Nothing about the meeting was decisive except the time it ended.§这次会议除了结束时间，没有什么是**决定性的**。
decode§The child decoded the first sentence and read no further.§孩子**破译**了第一句，就没再往下读。
decorative§Decorative brickwork hides a very plain frame.§**装饰**性的砖砌掩盖着极其朴素的框架。
decorous§A decorous distance was kept for the length of the ceremony.§整个仪式期间都保持着**得体**的距离。
decorum§Decorum in the reading room means whispering or not speaking at all.§阅览室的**礼仪**是要么低语，要么完全不说话。
decry§It is easy to decry a system you have never had to use.§**批判**一个你从未用过的制度很容易。
defective§The batch was defective in one respect only, and that one mattered.§这批产品只在一处**有缺陷**，而恰恰是那一处要紧。
defense§The best defense against a rumor is a published date.§对付谣言最好的**防卫**是公开的日期。
defensive§She was defensive about the draft and generous about the idea.§她对草稿很**戒备**，对这个想法却很大方。
defer§Junior staff deferred to him on everything except the schedule.§年轻员工在除日程之外的一切事上**都听他的**。
deferential§A deferential question is still a question.§**恭敬的**提问仍然是提问。
deferment§The deferment ran out and the debt came due in one week.§**展期**到头了，债务一周内就到期。
defiant§A defiant note was pinned to the door and left there for years.§一张**挑衅的**字条钉在门上，一挂就是好几年。
deficient§An argument deficient in dates is hard to check.§**缺少日期**的论证很难核实。
deficit§The rainfall deficit is measured against a thirty-year average.§降雨**亏缺**是以三十年平均值为基准衡量的。
definable§The boundary is definable on paper and invisible on the ground.§这条边界在纸上可以**界定**，在地面上却看不见。
define§Define your terms or the argument will define them for you.§要么你**界定**自己的术语，要么论证替你界定。
definitive§There is no definitive text; there are four competing ones.§没有**定本**，只有四个相互竞争的版本。
deflect§She deflected the question with a question of her own.§她用自己的一个问题把这个问题**挡了回去**。
defunct§The society is defunct and its records are in three counties.§这个协会**已不存在**，它的记录散在三个郡。
defy§He defied the ban and lectured in a rented hall.§他**无视禁令**，在一间租来的厅里讲课。
degenerate§Left unpruned, the orchard degenerates within five years.§不加修剪，果园五年内就会**退化**。
degeneration§Degeneration of the negative made the last print impossible.§底片的**老化**使最后一次冲印无法进行。
degradation§Plastic degradation in seawater takes centuries, not years.§塑料在海水中的**降解**需要几个世纪，而不是几年。
dehydrate§Dehydrate the sample fully before weighing it.§称重前请把样品彻底**脱水**。
delegate§A delegate from each district attended the vote.§每个区派一名**代表**参加表决。
deleterious§Even small doses proved deleterious over a long period.§即便小剂量，长期下来也证明**有害**。
deliberate§They deliberated for two days and returned without a verdict.§他们**审议**了两天，回来时仍未作出裁决。
deliberation§The deliberation was thorough and the outcome was predictable.§**审议**很充分，结果却在意料之中。
delineate§A single hedge delineates two counties.§一道树篱**划分出**两个郡。
delude§Do not be deluded by a well-designed cover.§别被精美的封面**骗了**。
delusion§It is a common delusion that older maps are more accurate.§认为旧地图更准确是一种常见的**错觉**。
demagogue§The demagogue and the reformer often start with the same complaint.§**煽动者**与改革者常常从同一个抱怨出发。
demanding§A demanding editor is a writer's best luck.§遇上一位**要求严格**的编辑，是作者最大的运气。
demean§Explaining your work does not demean it.§解释自己的作品并不会**贬低**它。
demise§Reports of the format's demise were premature by twenty years.§关于这种格式**消亡**的说法早说了二十年。
demographic§The magazine chased a demographic that had stopped reading magazines.§这本杂志追逐的**人群**早已不再读杂志。
demolish§One sentence in the appendix demolished the whole thesis.§附录里的一句话**摧毁**了整篇论文的立论。
demolition§Demolition was halted when a Roman floor appeared.§一块罗马时代的地面出现后，**拆除**就停了。
demonstration§A demonstration of three thousand people passed in silence.§三千人的**示威队伍**默默走过。
demonstrative§The pronoun here is demonstrative, not personal.§这里的代词是**指示**代词，不是人称代词。
demurral§His demurral was noted and then ignored.§他的**异议**被记录下来，随后就被忽视了。
denial§Denial of access to the archive lasted eleven years.§档案馆的查阅权**被拒绝**了十一年。
denotation§Two words with the same denotation may be impossible to swap.§两个**所指**相同的词可能完全不能互换。
denounce§To denounce a practice you profit from takes some nerve.§**谴责**一项自己从中获利的做法需要些胆量。
denude§A single winter denuded the bank of every plant.§一个冬天就把河岸上的植物**剥得精光**。
denunciation§The denunciation was anonymous and turned out to be accurate.§这份**告发**是匿名的，结果证明是准确的。
deny§I do not deny the figure; I question how it was reached.§我不**否认**这个数字，我质疑它是怎么得出的。
dependent§Two dependents were listed on the form and neither existed.§表格上列了两名**受抚养人**，两个都不存在。
depersonalize§The interface depersonalizes a decision that ruins someone's month.§这个界面把一个会毁掉别人一个月的决定弄得**毫无人情**。
depict§The map depicts the marsh as dry land, which it never was.§这幅地图把沼泽**画成**了旱地，而它从来不是。
depletion§Depletion of stocks was blamed on the weather for a decade.§库存的**耗竭**被归咎于天气长达十年。
